transcript:
Header: 2027-02-14 16:00 UTC | Duration: 47m | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (Valencia - Head of Search), Devon Park (Valencia - Sr ML Eng), Ravi Iyer (Valencia - Security), Jules (Procurement)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for making time, i'm Maya from Redwood Inference, with Liam our se, quick agenda: embeddings, similarity search, and our rerank endpoint plus q&a.
[00:12] Sofia: Great, quick context — we're redoing our site search for ecommerce catalogs, about 2-3 million SKUs, current stack is Elastic but relevancy drift and miss ranked products are big issue. latency target is sub 120ms P95 for search top-k.
[00:30] Liam: Cool. we'll show a hosted flow first — you call /embeddings for vectors, store them in your vector DB (or we can host), then when a query hits you can do a coarse recall using ANN then call our /rerank to score top candidates using model-context and prompt. we'll demo an example.
[00:46] Devon: are you suggesting we keep elastic for recall and use rerank for final ordering? That's our thought yes.
[00:55] Liam: Right, hybrid recall + rerank works well. you can also use our prefix/KV cache to speed repeated queries and reduce tokens. some notes — our runtime does continuous batching so burst efficiency improves cost.
[01:10] Ravi: security question — do you support SSO/SAML and KMS integration? all data must be encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys ideally.
[01:18] Maya: yes SOC 2, SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS/HSM integrations. we'll share the security whitepaper and key management doc after.
[01:28] Jules: procurement, rough pricing? we need cost ballpark for hosted POC (50k embeddings/day).
[01:35] Maya: we'll provide a POC pricing sheet; short answer — depends on embeddings dims & token throughput; Liam will run quick estimate once you share sample logs.

[02:05] --- Demo start ---
[02:06] Liam: all right i'm going to share my screen, starting with a quick curl to the embeddings endpoint. "curl POST /v1/embeddings" gives you a 1024-d vector per doc in this example, embedings are normalized, we return id/key, you store them in db.
[02:26] (slight audio overlap) Devon: are you returning float32 or quantized?
[02:30] Liam: by default float32 for precision; we also have quantization profiles for cost-lower inference and embeddings quant compression when you use Dedicated or Private, but hosted supports float32 & int8 reduction. note: embedings spelled embedings in some internal logs lol.
[02:46] Maya: small aside: we can recommend quantization policy after we see your similarity distribution.

[03:12] Liam: now rerank. simple flow: run ANN over store, get top 100 candidates, then call Redwood /rerank with query + doc snippets. rerank returns scores and an explain field if you enable structured output.
[03:30] Sofia: how many docs do customers usually send to rerank? 50-200?
[03:33] Liam: typically 20-200; recomended upper bound for low-latency is 100 candidates for wide web, but if you can accept 150-200 it's fine. The compute scales linearly of course.
[03:45] Devon: latency impact? our p95 SLA 120ms — can hosted meet that?
[03:50] Liam: depends on model & candidate count. for our smaller rerank model we see 60-80ms p95 for 50 candidates in hosted eu-west with streaming disabled. if you need guaranteed sub-120 we can either use a low-latency model variant or propose Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity. we'll run bench on your dataset.

[04:20] (15s silence while screenshare loads)
[04:37] Liam: demo time — sample query "red running shoes waterproof" — first we show vector recall results then rerank. sending rerank request... response: scores array, re-ordered top 5.
[04:58] Sofia: nice, what about attribute boosting (like price/promotions)? can we pass signals?
[05:05] Liam: yep you can pass structured features as part of rerank context, e.g., price, in_stock, promo_score; the model uses them as context but you can also do feature-based post-score mixing. we can show a small rule in console.

[06:12] Maya: question — do you have out-of-the-box metrics for A/B evals on rerank?
[06:18] Liam: Redwood Console provides per-route metrics, token usage, latency, and you can tie quality monitoring to prompt sets/evals to detect regressions. we'll show an example in the Console later.

[07:00] Devon: can we host embeddings with you or do we need our own vector DB?
[07:05] Liam: both — hosted flow we can manage vectors and provide an API-backed vector store, or you can continue using Elastic/Opensearch or Pinecone. many customers prefer keeping vectors in their infrastructure for compliance.

[07:40] Ravi: on compliance — if we do hosted and store vectors on Redwood, is there an option for customer-managed KMS?
[07:46] Maya: yes, for enterprise accounts we offer customer-managed KMS for hosted and for Private you bring your own HSM + on prem. we'll attach the KMS integration doc.

[08:10] Liam: a quick note on caching: prefix and KV cache reduce repeated token compute. in a search scenario we often cache rerank contexts for 1-5 minutes which helps cost for hot queries. but for freshness you can invalidate cache on catalog changes.

[08:45] Sofia: what about cold start jitter with batching? sometimes batching causes small tail latency spikes.
[08:50] Liam: true; our runtime has continuous batching and adaptive timeouts to balance latency and throughput; for strict p95 we can pin capacity on Dedicated or route low-latency queries to dedicated nodes.

[09:30] (customer asks for quick architecture diagram)
[09:34] Liam: i pulled up a simple flow: User -> App -> ANN recall (Elastic/Pinecone) -> topN -> Redwood /rerank -> ranked results. Alternative flow: send query to Redwood which handles both recall + rerank if you want unified stack.

[10:05] Sofia: does rerank support explainability? we'd like to see why results moved up or down for trust.
[10:12] Liam: we have an explain field — heuristic style plus model salience tokens, it's not formal proof but helps debugging. sometimes transcript picks up "explain" as "ex-plaine" by auto TTS.

[10:45] Liam: i'll run an on-the-fly benchmark: sending 100 requests with 50 candidates, using the small-re-rank model (internal name: redwood-rerank-small). results: median 48ms, p95 82ms, p99 180ms (p99 sensitive to larger contexts).
[11:12] Devon: p99 180 is high for us but p95 is fine; we care about p99 when running flash sales.
[11:20] Maya: you can configure fallback policies — if rerank exceeds threshold we can fall back to BM25 or your existing ranker. Redwood supports automatic fallback in the routing policies.

[12:00] Ravi: legal question — data retention and audit logs? we need retention policy + audit trails for queries & keys.
[12:07] Maya: Redwood provides audit logs, per-route tracing hooks and you can set retention policies; for Private you can keep logs on-prem.

[12:30] (small cross talk)
[13:00] Liam: switching to Console quick peek — per-route dashboards, token cost breakdown, and rollout controls like canary and A/B. you can compare two rerank models side-by-side.
[13:20] Sofia: can we do a canary where 10% traffic uses new rerank and compare clicks?
[13:24] Liam: yes you can do traffic split, and Console tracks quality metrics you define (CTR, session success).

[14:00] Devon: latency of Console operations? not critical but nice to know.
[14:04] Liam: Console is an ops plane; metrics dashboard has small lag for aggregated stats but traces are near real time.

[14:30] Maya: let's talk costs briefly: embeddings cost per 1k docs depends on vector dim and model; rerank cost largely token-based and candidate count. we'll give a sample calc in the spreadsheet.

[15:00] (customer asks about private deployment for regulatory needs)
[15:05] Ravi: we may eventually want Private deployment behind our VPC for European data residency. how does Redwood Private differ?
[15:12] Maya: Redwood Private gives you a private control plane and optionally on-prem package; networking is customer-managed, plus KMS/HSM and dedicated audit retention. Dedicated is hosted but reserved capacity. Private is best for strict residency.

[16:00] Liam: back to rerank specifics — request payload example: query, candidate_docs array (id, snippet, features), config flags (explain:true). responses include scores and optional structured explanation. small mis-typo in some earlier docs shows "candidate_docs" as "cand_docs" — we'll standardize in the SDKs.

[17:30] Sofia: curious about hallucinations in rerank — sometimes models hallucinate merch attributes.
[17:35] Liam: good point — rerank uses document context only; if snippet scraping was noisy you'll see hallucinations. fix by improving doc snippets, or use stricter deterministic signals (feature mixing). we also run quality monitors and regression alerts on eval prompt sets.

[18:40] Devon: is there support for embeddings incremental updates? our catalog updates hourly.
[18:44] Liam: yes incremental upserts are supported, and vector stores typically allow partial updates. we suggest a small TTL + background re-embed for heavy changes.

[19:20] Maya: we should capture a concrete POC scope — 2-week hosted POC, Valencia provides 50k sample docs + query logs + golden labels for a subset, Redwood runs rerank bench and provides results and cost estimate.
[19:34] Sofia: sounds good, 50k is doable. devon will send logs.

[20:00] (background noise)
[20:22] Liam: small note about deployment pins: you can pin model versions for rollouts and do canary percentage based. also auto fallback to cheaper variant if budget triggers.

[21:00] Ravi: for SOC2 audit, will you provide encryption attestations and key rotation logs?
[21:08] Maya: yes, rotation logs + KMS events are available; we'll include that in the security pack.

[22:20] (demo wraps with Q&A)
[22:30] Sofia: ok procurement question — what's the billing model for POC? prepay credits?
[22:36] Maya: we usually set up trial credits and a short term invoice for reserved test capacity if you want dedicated nodes. for hosted POC typically credits are fine.

[23:05] Liam: last tech note — rerank models have a small memory footprint; on Dedicated you can get better tail latency. also we expose kernel selection and quant profiles when you run on Private.

[24:00] Maya: recap: we'll send security docs (SOC2, KMS, SSO), Liam will run bench on sample data and share spreadsheet, Sofia will share sample logs and golden labels, and Ravi will confirm VPC constraints.

[24:20] Jules: procurement will look for contract term length and SLA options, will follow up via email.

[24:40] Maya: perfect, we'll also include a proposed POC plan in email with timeline.

[25:00] (small closing pleasantries)
[25:12] Sofia: thanks — this was super helpful.
[25:15] Devon: thanks everyone.
[25:20] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with docs and bench.

[25:35] (meeting ends; auto-trimmed last silence)
